name: Meshezabel
overview: Meshezabel was a male member of the tribe of Judah known primarily as the father of Pethahiah. His mention in Scripture is brief and focused on his genealogical role within the post-exilic community. There are no additional notes or significant events recorded about him beyond his lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Meshezabel means "G-d delivers," reflecting a theologically rich meaning common in Hebrew names, though it was not given directly by God. This name underscores a recognition of divine deliverance, which may reflect the faith context of his time.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Meshezabel as the father of Pethahiah and explicitly identifies him as a descendant of Zerah. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Meshezabel's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah during the post-exilic period. By being the father of Pethahiah and a descendant of Zerah, he is part of the restoration narrative that emphasizes the continuity of God's covenant people. His mention in Nehemiah 11:24 situates him within the community rebuilding Jerusalem, highlighting the faithfulness of God's people through generations.
